body.statement:
Fix \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), and put
\[
 \nu=\min\{1,\delta/R_{\max}\},
 \qquad
 \rho=\frac{\nu}{8+4\nu}.
\]
For every fixed \(0<\chi<\rho\), every deterministic integer sequence \(m_n\to\infty\), and every triangular array in \(\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)\), the randomized-jitter Gaussian-multiplier Anderson--Rubin set \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\) is implementable from the stratified observations and independent standard-normal draws and satisfies
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)}
 \left|
 \Pr_\theta\{\beta\in\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\}
 -(1-\alpha_0)
 \right|=0.
\]
This conclusion is uniform over influence covariance matrices whose ranks may change with \(n\), including the zero matrix, and uses neither an inverse nor a positive-eigenvalue bound for that covariance.  The jitter is \(n^{-\chi}\), hence vanishes on the root-\(n\) Anderson--Rubin scale underlying \(\mathcal C_n\).  By contrast, an unrandomized deterministic critical-value rule cannot in general be exactly calibrated at an atom: if the reference statistic has distribution function \(F\), a jump at \(q\), and \(1-\alpha_0\in(F(q-),F(q))\), neither strict nor weak deterministic thresholding at \(q\) has acceptance probability \(1-\alpha_0\).  Thus external randomization, or an assumption excluding such atoms, is necessary for the stated uniform exactness.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(W_{e,i}=(T_{e,i},Y_{e,i})\), and let \(q=(E-1)(R_{\max}-d-1)\), which is fixed.  The block maximum norm in the construction is one-Lipschitz with respect to the Euclidean norm.  All constants below depend only on the fixed coefficient, share, calibration-gap, and moment envelopes, never on the member of the triangular array.

At the true value \(b=\beta\), the uniform generated-projector expansion gives
\[
 H_n(\beta)=Z_n+R_n,\qquad
 Z_n=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
 \pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i}),                    \tag{1}
\]
where
\[
 \Sigma_n=\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\pi_e^{-1}
 \mathbb E[\zeta_{e,n}\zeta_{e,n}^{\top}]
\]
is positive semidefinite and may be singular.  Put
\[
 \nu=\min\{1,\delta/R_{\max}\}>0.
\]
The source moment envelope, the polynomial degree at most \(R_{\max}\) of every cumulant first projection, the coefficient bounds, and
\(\|C^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa_0^{-1}\) imply
\[
 \sup_{n,e,\theta}
 \mathbb E_\theta\|\zeta_{e,n}\|^{2+\nu}<\infty.     \tag{2}
\]
Here the displayed division is licensed by the calibration gap
\(\sigma_d(C)\geq\kappa_0>0\), and
\((2+\nu)R_{\max}\leq2R_{\max}+\delta\) licenses the moment in (2).

We first record a quantitative form of the singular Gaussian approximation; no covariance inverse is used.  Set
\[
 X_{e,i,n}=n^{-1/2}\pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i}).
\]
Balanced shares and (2) give
\[
 \sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
 \mathbb E_\theta\|X_{e,i,n}\|^{2+\nu}
 \leq K n^{-\nu/2}.                                 \tag{3}
\]
For a bounded one-Lipschitz function \(f\), convolve \(f\) with a
\(N(0,s^2I_q)\) density and call the result \(f_s\).  Direct
differentiation of that density and the Lipschitz property give
\[
 \|f_s-f\|_\infty\leq K_qs,\qquad
 [D^2f_s]_\nu\leq K_qs^{-1-\nu}.                    \tag{4}
\]
Replace the summands \(X_{e,i,n}\), one at a time, by independent
centered Gaussian vectors with the same covariance.  Taylor's formula
through order two cancels the means and covariances, and its integral
remainder is bounded by
\([D^2f_s]_\nu\|x\|^{2+\nu}/2\).  The Gaussian replacement has
\((2+\nu)\)-moment bounded by a dimension-dependent constant times the
corresponding covariance to the power \(1+\nu/2\), which is bounded by
the right side of (3) by Lyapunov's inequality.  Thus (3)--(4) yield
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L_\theta(Z_n),
 N(0,\Sigma_n)\right)
 \leq K\left(s+n^{-\nu/2}s^{-1-\nu}\right).          \tag{5}
\]
Taking \(s=n^{-\nu/(2(2+\nu))}\) makes the right side
\(O(n^{-\nu/(4+2\nu)})\), uniformly, including when \(\Sigma_n\) is
singular.

The proof of the generated-projector expansion also supplies an
explicit rate for its remainder.  The variance of every Hoeffding
projection of order at least two, after multiplication by \(n\), is
\(O(n^{-1})\).  For \(D_n=\widehat C-C\), the projector Taylor
remainder is bounded on
\(\{\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa_0/2\}\) by
\(K\sqrt n\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\), while
\[
 \Pr\{\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\kappa_0/2\}
 \leq4\kappa_0^{-2}\mathbb E\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 \leq K/n.                                          \tag{6}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[1\wedge
 \{\sqrt n\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\}\right]
 \leq\sqrt n\,\mathbb E\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 \leq K n^{-1/2}.                                   \tag{7}
\]
The products of two first-order estimation errors have the same bound
by Cauchy--Schwarz.  Equations (6)--(7), the higher-projection variance
bound, and (1) therefore imply
\[
 \sup_\theta
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L_\theta(H_n(\beta)),
 N(0,\Sigma_n)\right)
 \leq K n^{-\nu/(4+2\nu)}.                          \tag{8}
\]

We next verify that the multiplier law estimates the possibly singular
Gaussian law.  For an order-\(s\) kernel \(g\), conditional on
\(W_{e,i}\), the first term inside the brackets defining
\(\widehat\psi_{g,e,i}\) is an order-\((s-1)\) \(U\)-statistic for
\(\mathbb E[g(W_{e,i},W_2,\ldots,W_s)\mid W_{e,i}]\).
The overlap count used in the Hoeffding variance calculation and the
uniform square-integrability supplied by the moment envelope give
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
 \|\widehat\psi_{e,i}-\psi_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\|^2
 =O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1})                             \tag{9}
\]
uniformly, after stacking the finitely many cumulant coordinates.
The calibration gap and the projector expansion give
\[
 \|\widehat Q-Q_A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat C^\dagger-C^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 =O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}),                          \tag{10}
\]
and the exceptional branch in the definition of
\(\widehat C^\dagger\) has probability \(O(n^{-1})\) by (6).
Combining (9)--(10) with the bounded population cumulants yields
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{e,i}\pi_e^{-2}
 \|\widehat\zeta_{e,i}(\beta)-\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\|^2
 =O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1}).                            \tag{11}
\]

Conditionally on the data, \(G_n^{*(j)}(\beta)\) is exactly Gaussian
with covariance
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)
 =
 \frac1n\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
 \pi_e^{-2}
 \widehat\zeta_{e,i}(\beta)
 \widehat\zeta_{e,i}(\beta)^\top.                   \tag{12}
\]
To control (12) with only the maintained moments, put \(a=\nu/2\).
Each entry of
\(\zeta_{e,n}\zeta_{e,n}^{\top}\) has a uniformly bounded
\((1+a)\)-moment by (2).  Truncate its norm at
\[
 L_n=n^{1/(2(1+a))}.
\]
The truncation bias is at most \(K L_n^{-a}\).  The variance of the
average of the truncated independent matrices is at most
\(K L_n^{1-a}/n\), so its mean absolute deviation is at most
\(K n^{-1/2}L_n^{(1-a)/2}\).  Both terms equal, up to constants,
\[
 n^{-a/(2(1+a))}=n^{-\nu/(4+2\nu)}.                 \tag{13}
\]
The replacement error in (11) is smaller by Cauchy--Schwarz and the
tightness of the empirical second moments.  Therefore
\[
 \sup_\theta
 \mathbb E_\theta\!\left[
 1\wedge\|\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)-\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \right]
 \leq K n^{-\nu/(4+2\nu)}.                          \tag{14}
\]

For positive semidefinite matrices, the spectral calculus gives
\[
 \|S^{1/2}-T^{1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\|S-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{1/2}.                   \tag{15}
\]
This follows directly by applying the resolvent identity inside
\[
 S^{1/2}=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty
 t^{-1/2}S(S+tI)^{-1}\,dt
\]
and splitting the integral at
\(t=\|S-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\); thus (15) remains valid at zero
eigenvalues.  Couple the two Gaussian vectors as
\(\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)^{1/2}Z\) and
\(\Sigma_n^{1/2}Z\), where \(Z\sim N(0,I_q)\).  Equations (14)--(15)
and Jensen's inequality give
\[
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta\!
 \left[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L^*(G_n^{*(j)}(\beta)),N(0,\Sigma_n)
 \right)
 \right]
 \leq K n^{-\rho},
 \qquad \rho=\frac{\nu}{8+4\nu}.                    \tag{16}
\]
No rank condition on \(\Sigma_n\) or \(\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)\) has
entered (12)--(16).

It remains to handle atoms.  Let \(\tau_n=n^{-\chi}\) with
\(0<\chi<\rho\), let \(G_n\sim N(0,\Sigma_n)\), and define the ideal
smoothed distribution function
\[
 F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(t)
 =
 \Pr\{\|G_n\|_{\max}+\tau_n\xi\leq t\},
 \qquad \xi\sim N(0,1).
\]
For every \(t\), the map
\[
 x\longmapsto
 \Phi\!\left(\frac{t-\|x\|_{\max}}{\tau_n}\right)
\]
is bounded by one and has Lipschitz constant at most
\((\sqrt{2\pi}\tau_n)^{-1}\).  Hence (8) and (16) imply, respectively,
\[
 \sup_{\theta,t}
 \left|
 \Pr_\theta\{V_n(\beta)\leq t\}-F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(t)
 \right|\longrightarrow0,                          \tag{17}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta
 \sup_t\left|
 \Pr^*\{V_n^{*(j)}(\beta)\leq t\}
 -F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(t)
 \right|\longrightarrow0,                          \tag{18}
\]
because the right sides before taking limits are bounded by constants
times \(n^{\chi-\nu/(4+2\nu)}\) and
\(n^{\chi-\rho}\), respectively.  This is precisely why
\(\chi<\rho\) was imposed.

The distribution \(F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}\) is continuous and strictly
increasing even if \(G_n\) is supported on a proper subspace or equals
zero almost surely: its density is
\[
 t\longmapsto
 \mathbb E\left[
 \frac1{\tau_n}
 \phi\!\left(\frac{t-\|G_n\|_{\max}}{\tau_n}\right)
 \right]>0.                                         \tag{19}
\]
Consequently the probability integral transform applied to the ideal
variable has the exact uniform distribution.  The two uniform
Kolmogorov bounds (17)--(18), followed by the elementary inverse-CDF
inequalities, therefore show that the conditional Gaussian upper-tail
probability evaluated at \(V_n(\beta)\) converges in distribution,
uniformly over the shell, to a \(\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) variable.

Finally, conditional on the data and \(\xi_0\), the \(m_n\) indicators
in \(\widehat p_{n,m_n}(\beta)\) are independent Bernoulli variables.
If their common success probability is \(p_n^*(\beta)\), then
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(
 \frac1{m_n}\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}
 \mathbf 1\{V_n^{*(j)}(\beta)\geq V_n(\beta)\}
 \,\middle|\,\text{data},\xi_0
 \right)
 =
 \frac{p_n^*(\beta)\{1-p_n^*(\beta)\}}{m_n}
 \leq\frac1{4m_n}.                                  \tag{20}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality and \(m_n\to\infty\) make the simulated
upper-tail probability differ from \(p_n^*(\beta)\) by
\(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), uniformly.  Since
\(\alpha_0\in(0,1/2)\) is a continuity point of the uniform law,
(17)--(20) give
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)}
 \left|
 \Pr_\theta\{\widehat p_{n,m_n}(\beta)>\alpha_0\}
 -(1-\alpha_0)
 \right|\longrightarrow0.                          \tag{21}
\]
By the definition of the inversion set, the event in (21) is exactly
\(\{\beta\in\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\}\), proving the asserted
uniform exact coverage.  Also
\(\tau_n\xi_0=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), so the randomization vanishes on the
root-\(n\) Anderson--Rubin scale and does not replace the causal target
\(\beta\) by an observable functional.

To prove the obstruction for deterministic critical values, let \(F\)
be any reference distribution with a jump
\(\Delta=F(q)-F(q-)>0\) at \(q\).  Weak deterministic acceptance at
\(q\) has probability \(F(q)\), whereas strict deterministic
acceptance has probability \(F(q-)\).  If
\[
 F(q-)<1-\alpha_0<F(q),
\]
neither rule has the desired acceptance probability.  The explicit
extreme witness is a reference statistic equal to zero almost surely:
every deterministic threshold rule has acceptance probability zero
or one, never \(1-\alpha_0\).  Randomizing acceptance on the equality
event with probability
\[
 \frac{1-\alpha_0-F(q-)}{F(q)-F(q-)}
\]
would repair this atom exactly; the Gaussian jitter in
\(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\) is an implementable vanishing version
that does not require estimating the jump.  This proves both the
positive construction and the claimed necessity statement.
body.justification: External vanishing randomization converts the proved singular Gaussian approximation into exact, rather than merely conservative, null calibration.
body.gap: The same-sample estimated-plane correction is handled by the frozen influence expansion; the remaining atomic discontinuity is removed by an explicit vanishing Gaussian jitter.
body.consumer: The construction gives an implementable covariance-adaptive Anderson--Rubin confidence set for weak environmental cumulant flags.
